This article discusses women who have made an important contribution to the field of [physics](Physics "Physics").

## Physics awards

Female Nobel laureates in physics  
[Marie Curie](Marie_Curie "Marie Curie") – [Maria Goeppert Mayer](Maria_Goeppert_Mayer "Maria Goeppert Mayer")  
[Andrea Ghez](Andrea_Ghez "Andrea Ghez") – [Donna Strickland](Donna_Strickland "Donna Strickland")

### Nobel laureates

- 1903 [Marie Curie](Marie_Curie "Marie Curie"): "in recognition of the extraordinary services they have rendered by their joint researches on the radiation phenomena discovered by Professor [Henri Becquerel](Henri_Becquerel "Henri Becquerel")" [[1]](Women_in_physics#cite_note-1)
- 1963 [Maria Goeppert Mayer](Maria_Goeppert_Mayer "Maria Goeppert Mayer"): "for their discoveries concerning nuclear shell structure" [[2]](Women_in_physics#cite_note-2)
- 2018 [Donna Strickland](Donna_Strickland "Donna Strickland"): "for their method [high-intensity, ultra-short optical pulses](Chirped_pulse_amplification "Chirped pulse amplification")" [[3]](Women_in_physics#cite_note-3)
- 2020 [Andrea Ghez](Andrea_Ghez "Andrea Ghez"): "for the discovery of a [supermassive compact object](Sagittarius_A* "Sagittarius A*") at the centre of our galaxy."[[4]](Women_in_physics#cite_note-4)


Four women have won the [Nobel Prize in Physics](Nobel_Prize_in_Physics "Nobel Prize in Physics"), awarded annually since 1901 by the [Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences](Royal_Swedish_Academy_of_Sciences "Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences").[[5]](Women_in_physics#cite_note-TeshWade2017-5) [Marie Curie](Marie_Curie "Marie Curie") was the first woman to receive the prize in 1903, along with [Pierre Curie](Pierre_Curie "Pierre Curie") and [Henri Becquerel](Henri_Becquerel "Henri Becquerel") - making her the only woman to be awarded two Nobel prizes (her second Nobel prize was in Chemistry in 1911).[[6]](Women_in_physics#cite_note-nobelprize1911-6) [Maria Goeppert Mayer](Maria_Goeppert_Mayer "Maria Goeppert Mayer") became the second woman to win the prize in 1963, for her contributions to understanding the [nuclear shell structure](Nuclear_shell_model "Nuclear shell model"). [Donna Strickland](Donna_Strickland "Donna Strickland") was the third winner of the prize in 2018, for her work in [high-intensity, ultra-short optical pulses](Chirped_pulse_amplification "Chirped pulse amplification") beginning in the 1980s with [Gérard Mourou](G%C3%A9rard_Mourou "Gérard Mourou"). [Andrea Ghez](Andrea_Ghez "Andrea Ghez") was the fourth Nobel laureate in 2020, she shared one half of the prize with [Reinhard Genzel](Reinhard_Genzel "Reinhard Genzel") for the discovery of the supermassive compact object [Sagittarius A*](Sagittarius_A* "Sagittarius A*") at the center of our galaxy, the other half awarded to [Roger Penrose](Roger_Penrose "Roger Penrose") for theoretical work regarding [black hole](Black_hole "Black hole") formation.

Physicists and physicochemists that won a [Nobel Prize in Chemistry](Nobel_Prize_in_Chemistry "Nobel Prize in Chemistry") include Marie Curie,[[7]](Women_in_physics#cite_note-Nomination_Archive_–_Marie_Curie-7) [Irène Joliot-Curie](Ir%C3%A8ne_Joliot-Curie "Irène Joliot-Curie"), daughter of Marie Curie, in 1935,[[8]](Women_in_physics#cite_note-nobelprize.org2-8) and [Dorothy Hodgkin](Dorothy_Hodgkin "Dorothy Hodgkin") in 1964.[[9]](Women_in_physics#cite_note-ReferenceA2-9) Nuclear physicist [Rosalyn Sussman Yalow](Rosalyn_Sussman_Yalow "Rosalyn Sussman Yalow") was the second female scientist to win the [Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine](Nobel_Prize_in_Physiology_or_Medicine "Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine") in 1977 for the development of [radioimmunoassays](Radioimmunoassay "Radioimmunoassay").[[10]](Women_in_physics#cite_note-10)

### Nobel nominees

Other [physicists were nominated to the Nobel Prize in Physics](List_of_female_nominees_for_the_Nobel_Prize "List of female nominees for the Nobel Prize") but did not receive it, including:

- [Lise Meitner](Lise_Meitner "Lise Meitner"), nominated 19 times;[[11]](Women_in_physics#cite_note-Nomination_Archive_–_Lise_Meitner-11)
- [Marietta Blau](Marietta_Blau "Marietta Blau"), nominated 3 times;[[12]](Women_in_physics#cite_note-Nomination_Archive_–_Marietta_Blau-12)
